newsitem.title: USA: San Francisco voters OK bond, reject union measure.
newsitem.headline: San Francisco voters OK bond, reject union measure.

text.p: San Francisco voters approved a $100 million housing bond issue but slammed controversial measures that would have benefited local unions and given supervisors a pay raise, according to election returns.

Proposition A, a $100 million affordable housing bond measure, garnered the two-thirds vote it needed to pass. By contrast, Proposition B, a bond measure that would have raised $73.3 million to rebuild a San Francisco museum, fell four percentage points short.
Voters in the city also rejected a measure that would have allowed city workers to negotiate for retirement benefits. Voters also denied a pay raise to members of the Board of Supervisors.
